newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel set to vote on petroleum bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel set to vote on petroleum bill.

text.p: A final draft of a bill regulating the opening up of Brazil's petroleum industry to the private sector was due to be put to a vote in a committee in the Chamber of Deputies later Wednesday, officials said.

The committee was due to meet at 1000 local/1300 GMT to receive and vote on the latest version of the bill which would allow private companies to compete with state-owned Petrobras or go into partnership with it.
The bill would also allow foreigners to buy voting shares in Petrobras.
An aide to Dep. Eliseu Resende, who drew up the legislation, said the draft included alterations proposed by lawmakers in recent weeks but did not disclose those changes.
A congressional official said there was a possibility that members of the panel would ask for more time to study the bill, delaying today's scheduled vote.
If approved in the committee, the bill advances to the floor of the lower house. It also has to be approved in the Senate.
